title: Subdimensional linear-optical quantum computation: from qudit resource states to qubit quantum computation
abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear-optical quantum computation scheme that starts from high-dimensionally entangled qudits but performs quantum computation on qubits defined in their subspaces. This approach enables us to increase the success probability of linear-optical fusions from $50\%$ to $1-1/d$ for qudits of dimension $d$ without relying on existing approaches using ancilla photons and quantum codes. In particular, we show that a 2D cluster state of qubits can be generated from 5-qudit 1D cluster states using pairwise fusion gates while preserving their boosted success probability. We numerically demonstrate that this approach can improve the loss tolerance of a percolation-based scheme while keeping the photon number per resource state constant.
summary: This paper presents a quantum computation scheme for linear optics that utilizes high-dimensional qudits to enhance the success probability of fusion gates beyond the standard 50% limit. By employing pairwise fusion gates and adaptive measurements, the authors demonstrate a method to deterministically generate 2D cluster states from 1D states. This significantly improves the loss tolerance and scalability of measurement-based quantum computation in photonic systems.
main_problem: To develop a linear-optical quantum computation scheme that efficiently performs qubit computation using high-dimensionally entangled qudits.
main_result: The authors propose a method using pairwise fusion gates that boosts the success probability of linear-optical fusions from 50% to $1-1/d$, enabling the generation of 2D cluster states from 1D states.
method: The scheme employs a novel pairwise fusion gate (PFG) acting on qudits, combined with adaptive single-qudit measurements within a measurement-based quantum computation framework.
model_or_system: The physical platform is photonic quantum computation using linear-optical fusion gates. The theoretical framework extends the ZX calculus to qudit systems, utilizing qudits of dimension $d>2$.
key_observables: Fusion success probability, loss tolerance threshold, and the successful generation of 2D cluster states.
important_parameters: Qudit dimension ($d$), the success probability $1-1/d$, and the bond-percolation threshold (50%).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the ability to generate initial 1D cluster states deterministically and that the boosted fusion gates maintain their improved success probability.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates ZX-diagrammatic notations for qudits and subspaces. Figure 2 details the transformations achieved by adaptive measurements $	ext{Mc}$ and $	ext{Mm}$. Figure 3 shows the step-by-step process of generating 2D cluster states from 1D states using boosted fusion gates. Figure 4 presents the numerical results on the loss threshold for the percolation-based scheme.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of probabilistic fusion gates, proposes the PFG approach using qudits, details the use of adaptive measurements ($	ext{Mc}, 	ext{Mm}$) to generate 2D cluster states from 1D states, and finally analyzes the loss tolerance using a percolation-based scheme.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource efficiency and scalability in photonic quantum computation by leveraging higher-dimensional entanglement (qudits) to overcome inherent probabilistic limitations of linear optics.
